subject: High naive occupancy and N-mixture models

messages.author: afb61687c14423a1
messages.subject: High naive occupancy and N-mixture models
parts:
Hello unmarked community,

I'm starting with occupancy / abundance modeling and I have some questions about my data:

I have tried to understand the occupancy of giant anteater in a protected area. I modeled the single species single season occupancy with occu function at unmarked. The problem is that my models doesn't have a good fit (I do the GoF at modavg), all of them results in a high overdispersion (SE = NaN).
I think the sample size is too small (58 sites x 45 occasions) for the number of covariables I have (9 covariable site and 2 obs covariable).

There is some other occupancy model that my data fitted better?

Am I doing something wrong?

The naive occupancy is 0.72, so I thought that maybe could be a case of heterogeneous detection probability and the RN model could give me a better result. So, I tried to run it in unmarked with occuRN function and in fact I got good models. But this model measure the abundance, not the occupancy, so I want to know if I can use this model with the data I have (camera-traps records) and the species I work (a solitary species with large home range - about 9km² while my study area have 57km²). Maybe, the population there is too small.

To be clear, my question is: Is this model adequate for the data?

messages.author: 198c44d635827adf
messages.subject: Re: High naive occupancy and N-mixture models
parts:
Jessica,

The Royle-Nichols model typically produces better model fit with camera trap data because it accounts for heterogeneity in the detection data that isn't accounted for, which is extremely common for camera trap data. You can use the lambda2psi() function to convert the lambda estimate from the model to occupancy.
